title: Raw tympanogram asymmetry fails to improve hearing-difficulty prediction across NHANES recruitment cycles and an instrument change
abstract: We tested whether pressure-weighted raw-tympanogram skewness improves self-reported hearing-difficulty prediction beyond conventional tympanometric scalars, audiometric averages and demographics. Source-only models in NHANES2011–2012 (n=3582) were evaluated in separately recruited2015–2016 (n=3840), after prefit harmonization of Earscan and Titan pressure grids. Adding mean bilateral absolute skewness changed target MEC-weighted Brier score from 0.122102 to 0.122883, delta +0.000781; joint rescaled-PSU bootstrap95% interval [-0.000910,+0.002096]. The registered benefit criterion was not met. This negative result applies to a specific shape statistic under joint recruitment/instrument transfer, not to all raw-curve information or within-instrument performance.
